description: Threat actors tools is an enumeration of tools used by adversaries. The list includes malware but also common software regularly used by the adversaries.
name: Trellix Star - Tool

values.description:
7-Zip is a popular file compression and archiving utility that allows users to compress and decompress files and folders efficiently. It is known for its high compression ratio, which means it can create smaller file sizes compared to other compression tools. The software uses its own compression format called 7z, but it also supports various other file formats for both compression and extraction, including ZIP, RAR, TAR, GZIP, and more. It is available for Windows operating systems, but there are also unofficial versions and command-line versions that work on Linux and macOS. 

One of the key features of 7-Zip is its ability to compress files into the 7z format with a higher compression ratio than most other compression tools. This can be particularly useful when you need to save disk space or transfer files over the internet. It achieves this high compression ratio through the use of advanced compression algorithms, such as LZMA and LZMA2.

AdFind is a free command-line query tool that can be used for gathering information from Active Directory.

Source: MITRE

ADVobfuscator demonstates how to use C++11/14 language to generate, at compile time, obfuscated code without using any external tool and without modifying the compiler. The technics presented rely only on C++11/14, as standardized by ISO. It shows also how to introduce some form of randomness to generate polymorphic code and it gives some concrete examples like the encryption of strings literals and the obfuscation of calls using finite state machines.

Source: https://github.com/andrivet/ADVobfuscator

Awk is a scripting language used for manipulating data and generating reports. The awk command programming language requires no compiling and allows the user to use variables, numeric functions, string functions, and logical operators. 

Awk is a utility that enables a programmer to write tiny but effective programs in the form of statements that define text patterns that are to be searched for in each line of a document and the action that is to be taken when a match is found within a line. Awk is mostly used for pattern scanning and processing. It searches one or more files to see if they contain lines that matches with the specified patterns and then perform the associated actions.

Source: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/awk-command-unixlinux-examples/

Babuk is a Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) malware that has been used since at least 2021. The operators of Babuk employ a "Big Game Hunting" approach to targeting major enterprises and operate a leak site to post stolen data as part of their extortion scheme.
Source: MITRE

BadRentdrv2 is a malicious, vulnerable driver that operates on both 32-bit and 64-bit systems. It poses a significant security threat by actively disabling and terminating various widespread endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions and antivirus programs, ultimately leaving target systems entirely unprotected.

Bash is the GNU Project's shell—the Bourne Again SHell. This is an sh-compatible shell that incorporates useful features from the Korn shell (ksh) and the C shell (csh). It is intended to conform to the IEEE POSIX P1003.2/ISO 9945.2 Shell and Tools standard. It offers functional improvements over sh for both programming and interactive use. In addition, most sh scripts can be run by Bash without modification.

Source: https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/

Boot Configuration Data (BCD) files provide a store that is used to describe boot applications and boot application settings.

BCDEdit is a command-line tool for managing BCD. It can be used for a variety of purposes, including creating new stores, modifying existing stores, and adding boot menu options.

Threat actors may use BCDEdit to disable recovery features

BeeFlush is a web shell that uses Java to read and decode data from a web traffic parameter named Fushd. It then joins the decoded data with a command that redirects the output stream for execution through /bin/sh. After the command is run, BeeFlush reads the resulting input stream, base64 encodes the information, and then writes it back out as the response.

The Black Basta Ransomware is a significant cyber threat targeting organizations, not individual users, by encrypting their data. This ransomware employs an encryption algorithm that renders locked files unrecoverable without the proper decryption keys. Upon encryption, it renames files by appending the '.basta' extension, changes the desktop background, and leaves a ransom note named 'readme.txt' on the compromised system.

Bobik offers remote access capabilities but also has a DDoS module that was used against supporters of Ukraine.

Source: malpedia

BrickStorm is a Go-based backdoor specifically designed to target VMware vCenter servers. This malware possesses a range of capabilities, including the ability to establish itself as a web server, manage files and directories, upload and download files, execute shell commands, and facilitate SOCKS relaying. Communication with its command-and-control server is conducted over WebSockets to a predefined C2 address.

The BushWalk webshell is written in Perl and is embedded into a legitimate CS file. The malware provides a threat actor the ability to read or write files to a server.

Source: Mandiant

BusyBox is an open-source software suite that provides several Unix utilities in a single executable file that was initially released in November 1999. It combines tiny versions of many common UNIX utilities into a single small executable and provides a fairly complete environment for small or embedded system. The author's had dubbed it as "The Swiss Army Knife of Embedded Linux" and as single executable replaces basic functions of more than 400 common commands.Threat actors might misuse and try to upload this on Internet of Things (IOT) devices to facilitate further compromise.

CASTLETAP is a passive backdoor that listens for a specialized ICMP packet for activation.

Source: Mandiant

cat is a standard Unix utility that reads files sequentially, writing them to standard output. The name is derived from its function to concatenate files. It has been ported to a number of operating systems.
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_(Unix)

ChainLine is a Python web shell backdoor that is embedded in a Ivanti Connect Secure Python package that enables arbitrary command execution.

Source: Mandiant

The chcon command in Linux is used to change the SELinux (Security-Enhanced Linux) context of a file or directory. SELinux uses a security context, which includes labels like user, role, type, and level, to enforce access controls. The chcon command allows users to modify these labels.

The `chmod` command and system call in Unix and Unix-like operating systems allows users to modify the access permissions of file system objects such as files and directories. Beyond basic read, write, and execute permissions, this utility is also responsible for altering special mode flags, which include setuid, setgid, and the sticky flag, thereby controlling how the system handles file execution and directory access.
Windows command interpreter, Cmd.exe. If used without parameters, cmd displays the version and copyright information of the operating system. Source: Microsoft

Cobalt Strike, a commercial penetration testing framework, enables the deployment of an agent named 'Beacon' on a compromised system. Beacon provides extensive capabilities to the attacker, encompassing command execution, keylogging, file transfer, SOCKS proxying, privilege escalation, mimikatz, port scanning, and lateral movement. Operating in-memory and filelessly, Beacon utilizes stageless or multi-stage shellcode, which upon execution via a vulnerability or shellcode loader, loads itself directly into a process's memory without disk interaction. It supports command and control (C2) and staging over various protocols, including HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, SMB named pipes, and TCP, with both forward and reverse connections, and allows for daisy-chaining of Beacons. The framework includes Artifact Kit, a toolkit designed for crafting shellcode loaders. The Beacon implant's popularity among threat actors stems from its robust design, stability, and extensive customization options.

The Conti ransomware family was discovered in 2020 and uses numerous techniques to find files to attack and to carry out the encryption process.

The malware uses multiple threads to encrypt files at a faster rate compared to other ransomware families and contains command-line options to scan for local files as well as remote files over SMB shares. Conti uses the Windows Restart Manager to free up files that are opened by various applications and vssadmin to delete the Windows Volume Shadow Copies. The malware uses over 100 commands to stop Microsoft Windows services and terminates any process with "sql" in the name. Conti uses AES-256 encryption and requires the victim to email the threat actor for the decryption key.

Variants of the malware post stolen data from entities who refuse to pay the ransom.

Various malicious and non-malicious tools have been used to distribute Conti including Cobalt Strike, PsExec, Trickbot, Emotet, and BazarLoader.

Conti is delivered to victims in a variety of ways including open RDP connections, phishing, and the exploitation of software vulnerabilities.

CrackMapExec, or CME, is a post-exploitation tool developed in Python and designed for penetration testing against networks. CrackMapExec collects Active Directory information to conduct lateral movement through targeted networks.

Source: MITRE

Curl is a command-line tool for transferring data specified with URL syntax.
Source: https://github.com/curl/curl

DarkGate, a commodity loader initially documented in 2018, possesses functionalities such as downloading and executing files directly into memory, a Hidden Virtual Network Computing (HVNC) module, keylogging, information exfiltration capabilities, and privilege escalation. Leveraging legitimate AutoIt files, DarkGate typically executes multiple AutoIt scripts concurrently. Advertisements for new versions of DarkGate have been observed on a Russian-language eCrime forum since May 2023.

values.description:
DDOSIA is a multi-threaded application that conducts denial-of-service attacks against target sites by repeatedly issuing network requests. DDOSIA issues requests as instructed by a configuration file that the malware receives from a C2 server when started. The configuration file is in JSON format and resides at the /client/get_targets URL path on the C2 server.

Source: SentinelOne

DRIEDMOAT is a passive backdoor that has been observed with an embedded certificate stolen from the compromised appliance that it uses to encrypt its C2 communications.

Source: Google

DSLog is a webshell exploiting the Ivanti Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability (CVE-2024-21893), providing remote access to compromised devices. Evidence of exploitation is found in Ivanti logs, where unauthenticated actors issue SAML authentication requests containing encoded commands. The script checks for modifications to the 'DSLog.pm' Perl script, used for logging events, by searching for 'HTTP_USER_AGENT'. If absent, the backdoor is injected using the 'sed' command at line 102 of the 'DSLog.pm' file.

In computing, echo is a command that outputs the strings that are passed to it as arguments. It is a command available in various operating system shells and typically used in shell scripts and batch files to output status text to the screen or a computer file, or as a source part of a pipeline.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echo_(command)

enum4linux is a Linux alternative to enum.exe for enumerating data from Windows and Samba hosts.

Source: https://labs.portcullis.co.uk/tools/enum4linux/

The esxcli tool serves as the central command line interface for the administration and diagnostic analysis of VMware ESXi hosts. It utilizes a structured hierarchy of namespaces to categorize operations based on specific functional areas, which allows administrators to efficiently navigate through tasks related to networking, storage, and system configurations. By providing a comprehensive set of commands within this organized framework, the utility enables precise control over the host environment and simplifies the process of resolving technical issues.

FrameSting is a Python web shell embedded in a Ivanti Connect Secure Python package that enables arbitrary command execution.

Source: Mandiant

fsutil performs tasks that are related to file allocation table (FAT) and NTFS file systems, such as managing reparse points, managing sparse files, or dismounting a volume. If it's used without parameters, fsutil displays a list of supported subcommands.

Source: Microsoft
Garble is an open-source tool used to obfuscate Golang-based binaries.
gdrive is a command line application for interacting with Google Drive.

GhostLocker is a sophisticated ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) framework developed by the GhostSec hacktivist group and promoted through a Telegram channel at an initial price of $999.00. The ransomware builder offers several options to select from such as kill processes, disable services, ransom amount, directories to encrypt, remove background, and delete malicious binaries.

Source: Uptycs

mitre-attack: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder - T1547.001

values.description: GhostPresser is a tool associated with the GhostSec threat group. It functions as an admin bypass and hacking tool specifically targeting the WordPress content management system. This shell script was allegedly utilized by GhostSec in an XSS attack against legitimate websites.

The GhostSec deep scan toolset is a Python utility that an attacker can use to scan the websites of their potential targets.

Source: Cisco

GHOSTTOWN is a utility used by the suspected China-nexus cyber espionage actor UNC3886.

Source: Google

GitHub is a web-based platform used for version control and collaboration on software development projects. It provides tools for developers to host and review code, manage projects, track changes, and collaborate with other team members or contributors. GitHub uses Git, a distributed version control system, allowing developers to track changes made to code over time, revert to previous versions if needed, and work on code collaboratively with others. It is widely used by individuals, open-source projects, and businesses to streamline software development processes and facilitate collaboration among developers worldwide.

GlassToken is a custom web shell seen on external facing servers. The web shell contains two functions, the first is to act as a tunnel, using code borrowed from reGeorg, the second is custom code to execute arbitrary .NET code.

Source: Volexity
Google Drive is a cloud-based storage service used to store files.

Package gorilla/mux implements a request router and dispatcher for matching incoming requests to their respective handler.

Source: https://github.com/gorilla/mux

grep searches for PATTERNS in each FILE. PATTERNS is one or more patterns separated by newline characters, and grep prints each line that matches a pattern. Typically PATTERNS should be quoted when grep is used in a shell command.
Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/grep.1.html

The GrimBolt backdoor is a persistent access tool developed in C# that utilizes native ahead-of-time compilation and UPX packing to enhance its stealth and efficiency. This malicious software is designed to establish a reliable foothold within a compromised environment, primarily serving to facilitate remote shell capabilities for unauthorized operators. By leveraging these specific compilation and compression techniques, the malware complicates detection efforts while ensuring a direct command-line interface for remote execution.

GuestConduit is a Golang-based implant designed for network traffic tunneling that operates within a guest virtual machine (VM). It establishes a VSOCK listener on port 5555 to enable communication between the guest VM and the hypervisor. GuestConduit is also capable of parsing JSON-formatted client requests to either mirror or forward network traffic and appears to be designed to integrate with Junction's tunneling functionalities.

Gzip is a single-file/stream lossless data compression utility, where the resulting compressed file generally has the suffix .gz. Gzip also refers to the associated compressed data format used by the utility.

Source: https://www.gzip.org/

Heroku is a cloud platform as a service that enables developers to build, run, and operate applications entirely in the cloud. It simplifies the process of deploying and scaling software by managing the underlying infrastructure, such as servers and databases, allowing developers to focus solely on writing code. The platform supports a wide variety of programming languages and provides a straightforward workflow for pushing code from development to a live production environment. This makes it a popular choice for developers looking for a fast and efficient way to get their applications online without extensive system administration knowledge.

IcedID, also referred to as BokBot, is a modular banking trojan designed to exfiltrate user financial data and function as a dropper for additional malware. Employing a man-in-the-browser attack vector, it captures sensitive financial information, including login credentials for active online banking sessions. Upon successful initial compromise, IcedID utilizes the stolen data to assume control of banking accounts and execute automated fraudulent transactions. Primarily disseminated as a secondary payload by other malware, notably Emotet, and through its own malspam campaigns, IcedID employs various injection techniques, such as injecting itself into operating system (OS) memory and legitimate processes, to bypass antivirus and other malware detection mechanisms. The malware's developers actively update IcedID to enhance persistence and evade evolving detection efforts.

ImageMagick is a free and open-source software suite for displaying, converting, and editing raster image and vector image files. It can read and write over 200 image file formats, and can support a wide range of image manipulation operations, such as resizing, cropping, and color correction.

Source: https://imagemagick.org/

Impacket serves as a comprehensive open-source library of Python modules designed for the programmatic construction and manipulation of various network protocols. It provides a sophisticated framework for security professionals to perform a wide range of tasks, including the execution of remote services, manipulation of Kerberos tickets, and extraction of Windows credentials. Furthermore, the toolkit facilitates network traffic analysis through packet sniffing and supports the implementation of complex relay attacks, making it a versatile asset for evaluating and managing network security environments.

mitre-attack: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay - T1557.001

values.description:
Interactsh is an Open-Source Solution for Out of band Data Extraction, A tool designed to detect bugs that cause external interactions, For example - Blind SQLi, Blind CMDi, SSRF, etc.

Source: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh

The Invoke-Expression cmdlet executes a provided string as a command, returning the output of the evaluated expression or command. In the absence of Invoke-Expression, a string entered at the command line is simply echoed back without interpretation or execution.

Iodine lets you tunnel IPv4 data through a DNS server. This can be usable in different situations where internet access is firewalled, but DNS queries are allowed.

Source: https://github.com/yarrick/iodine

Displays all current TCP/IP network configuration values and refreshes Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) and Domain Name System (DNS) settings. Used without parameters, ipconfig displays the IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway for all adapters.

Source: Microsoft

iptables is a powerful and flexible firewall utility used in Linux-based operating systems to control network traffic by defining rules and policies. It allows system administrators to set up rules for packet filtering, network address translation (NAT), and packet mangling. With iptables, you can define which packets are allowed or blocked based on various criteria such as source and destination IP addresses, ports, protocols, and packet state.

JavaScript, often abbreviated as JS, is a programming language that conforms to the ECMAScript specification. JavaScript is high-level, often just-in-time compiled and multi-paradigm. It has dynamic typing, prototype-based object-orientation and first-class functions.

JavaScript is used for web development, in web applications, for game development, and much more. It allows you to implement dynamic features on web pages that cannot be done with only HTML and CSS. Many browsers use JavaScript as a scripting language for doing dynamic things on the web. Any time you see a click-to-show dropdown menu, extra content added to a page, and dynamically changing element colours on a page, to name a few features, you're seeing the effects of JavaScript.

Exploiting JavaScript in cyber attacks is not exactly new, but the increasing frequency of this attack vector is. Even in 2020, JavaScript-based attacks are still a matter of great concern. The danger in these attacks lies in one key aspect: malware delivered via infected JavaScript files doesn’t need user interaction. Better said, a user could get infected with malware without doing anything else than browsing a website. JavaScript is not an insecure programming language, code bugs or improper implementations can create backdoors which attackers can exploit.

Junction is implemented in Golang and targets VMware ESXi servers, operating under the guise of a legitimate ESXi service. It listens on port 8090, a port shared with the authentic VMware vvold service. Junction functions as an HTTP server, processing inbound requests, and possesses a broad range of capabilities. These capabilities encompass command execution, network traffic proxying, and inter-VM communication via VM sockets (VSOCK).

Kubo Injector is a library for injecting a shared library into a Linux, Windows and MacOS process.

Source: https://github.com/kubo/injector

LaZagne is a post-exploitation, open-source tool used to recover stored passwords on a system. It has modules for Windows, Linux, and OSX, but is mainly focused on Windows systems. LaZagne is publicly available on GitHub.

LightWire is a web shell written in Perl CGI that is embedded into a legitimate Secure Connect file to enable arbitrary command execution. LIGHTWIRE intercepts requests to compcheckresult.cgi that contain the parameters “comp=comp” and “compid”, where “compid” contains Base64-encoded and RC4-encrypted ciphertext. The decoded cleartext is interpreted and executed as Perl code.

Source: Mandiant

LittleLamb.WoolTea is a backdoor linked to UNC5325. It possesses a feature for maintaining persistence through system upgrades and patches. Upon execution, the malware triggers the first_run() function, which examines the appliance's hardware by accessing the first four bytes of the motherboard serial number located at /proc/ive/mbserialnumber. Based on this information, it adapts its actions to mount the root partition of the factory reset image for subsequent modifications.

Living-off-the-land binaries, or LoLBins, are used by multiple threat actors to appear legitimate and stay under the radar of security researchers. The dual-use tools are used by adversaries to execute arbitrary code, bypass security controls, dump memory, log keystrokes, and steal credentials. The binaries are also used to upload sensitive information and download additional malware onto the infected systems.

The Lockbit Ransomware-as-a-Service was identified in the first quarter of 2020 by a joint research effort between McAfee Labs and Northwave. Initial access is carried out with phishing campaigns or by brute-forcing external services. After gaining access the malware uses privileged accounts for reconnaissance and to move laterally throughout the network. For defense evasion the malware disables security applications and any other tools which could render a successful infection. Once a victim is compromised, a ransom note is dropped by the malware reporting that, in addition to encrypting files, the threat actor has also exfiltrated private data including financial, personal, and network information. The ransom note further instructs the victim to a dark web address to regain access to their encrypted data. The actor behind the malicious software has threatened to publish the exfiltrated confidential data if the ransom is not met within the set time frame.

LOOKOVER is a sniffer written in C that processes TACACS+ authentication packets, performs decryption, and writes its contents to a specified file path. LOOKOVER uses the publicly available libpcap library to sniff TCP packets.

Source: Google

Mario ransomware is operated by Ransom House, a group that emerged in 2021. Ransom House initially claimed that they target vulnerable networks to steal data without encrypting files. However, the group has since adopted cryptographic lockers. The verbose ransom note content is the most unique part of Mario’s ESXi locker. The Ransom House actors provide very explicit instructions to the victim explaining what to do and how to contact the actors.

Source: SentinelOne

Medusa is a small, modular Linux rootkit compiled as an ELF executable that deploys without extra building or configuration to gain complete system control. Upon execution, it configures a dynamic linker to modify application loading and hooks a wide range of system calls, library functions, and signal handlers to establish persistent, stealthy access. By intercepting these system calls, Medusa manipulates system behavior to control file access, mask permissions, alter read and write operations, modify file properties, and intercept user login and account information.

The Metasploit Project, owned by Rapid7, is a computer security project that provides information about security vulnerabilities and aids in penetration testing and IDS signature development. The open-source Metasploit Framework, a tool for developing and executing exploit code against a remote target machine, is its most renowned sub-project. Other significant sub-projects include the Opcode Database, shellcode archive, and related research. The Metasploit Project also encompasses anti-forensic and evasion tools, some of which are integrated into the Metasploit Framework. Additionally, Metasploit comes pre-installed in the Kali Linux operating system.

Mimikatz is a powerful, open-source tool that's primarily used to extract credentials, such as passwords, from Windows systems. It allows users to retrieve sensitive information from memory, which can then be used for malicious purposes like unauthorized access and lateral movement within a network. While it's used by security professionals for penetration testing, it's also a common tool in the hands of cybercriminals.
MiniDump is a hacking tool employed to extract credentials by dumping the memory of the LSASS process.

The mkdir command is a standard command-line utility used to create new directories, or folders, within the file system of Microsoft Windows operating systems. By executing this command in the Command Prompt or PowerShell, users can quickly generate single or nested directories at a specified path, streamlining the process of file organization without needing to use the graphical user interface.

MOPSLED is a shellcode-based modular backdoor that has the capability to communicate over HTTP or a custom binary protocol over TCP to its C2 server. The core functionality of MOPSLED involves expanding its capabilities by retrieving plugins from the C2 server. MOPSLED also uses a custom ChaCha20 encryption algorithm to decrypt embedded and external configuration files.

Source: Google

In computing, mount is a command in various operating systems. Before a user can access a file on a Unix-like machine, the file system on the device[1] which contains the file needs to be mounted with the mount command. Frequently mount is used for SD card, USB storage, DVD and other removable storage devices. The command is also available in the EFI shell.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_(Unix)

MrAgent is a malware tool used to automate ransomware deployment on ESXi hypervisors. It provides remote access to compromised hosts, allowing threat actors to disable security controls and operate mass encryption. MrAgent gathers information on virtual environments and tracks ransomware execution across infected hypervisors.

Neo-reGeorg is an advanced network tunneling tool designed as an aggressive refactor of reGeorg to improve performance, stealth, and cross-platform compatibility in challenging environments. It enhances security and evasion by encrypting transmissions via modified base64 encoding disguised as standard base64, utilizing a Byte-LengthOffset-Value data format, randomized URL requests, and customizable HTTP headers, status codes, and error pages. Built to run seamlessly across Python 2 and 3, it offers robust resilience against unstable server setups and load-balanced architectures through features like server-side DNS resolution, intranet forwarding, process-based server startup, session-independent operation for non-PHP platforms, and multi-TCP connection creation for PHP scenarios.

Netsh is a command-line scripting utility that allows you to, either locally or remotely, display or modify the network configuration of a computer that is currently running. Netsh also provides a scripting feature that allows you to run a group of commands in batch mode against a specified computer. Netsh can also save a configuration script in a text file for archival purposes or to help you configure other servers.
Source: Microsoft

mitre-attack: Disable or Modify System Firewall - T1562.004

values.description:
Displays active TCP connections, ports on which the computer is listening, Ethernet statistics, the IP routing table, IPv4 statistics (for the IP, ICMP, TCP, and UDP protocols), and IPv6 statistics (for the IPv6, ICMPv6, TCP over IPv6, and UDP over IPv6 protocols). Used without parameters, netstat displays active TCP connections.

 Source: Microsoft.

nex is a library that aims to simplify the construction of JSON API service, nex.Handler is able to wrap any function to adapt the interface of http.Handler, which unmarshals POST data to a struct automatically.

Source: https://github.com/lonng/nex

Nmap ('Network Mapper') is a free and open source (license) utility for network discovery and security auditing. Many systems and network administrators also find it useful for tasks such as network inventory, managing service upgrade schedules, and monitoring host or service uptime. Nmap uses raw IP packets in novel ways to determine what hosts are available on the network, what services (application name and version) those hosts are offering, what operating systems (and OS versions) they are running, what type of packet filters/firewalls are in use, and dozens of other characteristics. It was designed to rapidly scan large networks, but works fine against single hosts. Nmap runs on all major computer operating systems, and official binary packages are available for Linux, Windows, and Mac OS X. In addition to the classic command-line Nmap executable, the Nmap suite includes an advanced GUI and results viewer (Zenmap), a flexible data transfer, redirection, and debugging tool (Ncat), a utility for comparing scan results (Ndiff), and a packet generation and response analysis tool (Nping).

NordVPN is a VPN service provided by company Nordsec Ltd with applications for Microsoft Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, and Android TV. Manual setup is available for wireless routers, NAS devices, and other platforms.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NordVPN

Nuitka functions as a comprehensive replacement or extension for the Python interpreter by compiling all language constructs available across a wide range of versions from CPython 2.6 through 3.10. When executed with a specific Python version, it maintains rigorous compatibility by allowing uncompiled and compiled code to operate together seamlessly. This approach ensures that the original behavior of the software is preserved while providing the benefits of a compiled environment.

PIA Proxy is a service offering access to a large network of residential SOCKS5 proxies from many different countries. It allows users to route their internet traffic through these diverse IP addresses for tasks such as web data scraping, ad verification, and managing multiple online accounts.

Pikabot is a malicious backdoor that has been active since early 2023. The malware is modular with a loader and a core component that implements the majority of the functionality. Pikabot is capable of receiving commands from a command-and-control server such as the injection of arbitrary shellcode, DLLs or executable files.

Source: Zscaler

mitre-attack: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder - T1547.001

values.description: The ping utility is a primary network diagnostic tool that utilizes the Internet Control Message Protocol to verify connectivity between devices. When executed, it sends an Echo Request packet to a specified IP address or hostname and waits for an Echo Reply to measure the total round-trip time. This process allows users to determine if a remote host is active and helps identify issues such as packet loss or high latency within a network path. By providing immediate feedback on the stability and speed of a connection, it serves as an essential first step for troubleshooting communication errors across both local and wide area networks.

PitDog is a malicious SparkGateway plugin employing Kubo Injector to insert a shared object into web process memory, enabling persistent execution of a backdoor. It is activated during RDP connection negotiation, triggered by the Handshake plugin invocation. The getHandshakePlugin() method initiates a new thread from a Runnable interface, which iteratively calls SparkPlugin.watchdog() every ten (10) seconds. This approach ensures the continuous operation of the malicious watchdog method without disrupting the primary functionality of the SparkGateway application, serving as a persistence mechanism.

PitFuel is a SparkGateway plugin that loads the shared object libchilkat.so (LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA) through the Java Native Interface (JNI) by calling System.load(). The shared object persistently deploys backdoors and contains capabilities to persist across system upgrade events, patches, and factory resets.

Source: Mandiant

PitHook, linked to UNC5325, is a backdoor that intercepts the accept and accept4 functions in the web process by altering the PLT. Upon detecting a buffer matching a predetermined magic byte sequence, it duplicates the socket and initiates communication with the Unix domain socket /data/runtime/cockpit/wd.fd.

PitSock, associated with UNC5325, is a backdoor that intercepts the accept and setsockopt functions of the web process by altering its procedure linkage table (PLT). Through this modification, it establishes communication via the Unix socket /tmp/clientsDownload.sock upon receiving a predefined 48-byte magic byte sequence in the incoming buffer.

PitStop, associated with UNC5325, is a backdoor that monitors the Unix domain socket at /data/runtime/cockpit/wd.fd, initialized by PitHook upon receiving a predetermined magic byte sequence. It duplicates the socket for communication over TLS. Upon socket establishment, PitStop utilizes Base64 encoding and a fixed AES key to interpret incoming commands. It supports execution of shell commands, file writing, and file reading on the compromised device.

Microsoft's powershell scripting language is available by default from Windows 7 upwards and therefore provides stealth with that environment for launching attacks. Further, powershell has been made open-source and cross-platform with the advent of 'powershell core' in 2016.

PowerShell provides full access to all Windows services including Microsoft COM (Component Object Model) and Microsoft Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI), while add-ins can easily be imported to include functionality for managing Active Directory, Exchange, etc.

Some other features that make powershell an interesting choice for attackers include:
 - Ability to run code directly in memory with ease
 - Flexibility to encode elements of a script in a multitude of ways
 - Full access to the Microsoft .Net framework
 - Ability to re-create the powershell framework binary using .Net framework dll's.
 - Logging and detecting behavior is difficult in older versions
 - Availability of a number of quality attack frameworks written in powershell.

Source: Microsoft

The printf command in Linux is used to display the given string, number or any other format specifier on the terminal window. It works the same way as “printf” works in programming languages like C.

Source: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/printf-command-in-linux-with-examples/

PrivadoVPN is a virtual private network service that focuses on user privacy and security, operating under Swiss privacy laws which are known for being stringent. It offers both a free and a paid subscription, with the free version providing a limited amount of data each month. The service encrypts users' internet traffic, hides their IP address, and follows a strict no-logs policy, meaning it does not track or store online activity. Key features include a kill switch to prevent data leaks if the VPN connection drops, a selection of secure VPN protocols, and servers located in various countries around the world. It is designed to enable access to geographically restricted content and provide a secure connection, especially when using public Wi-Fi networks.

PySoxy is an open-source tool written in Python that functions as a SOCKS5 proxy server to facilitate network traffic routing. It provides a lightweight and accessible solution for users looking to implement or study proxy protocols within a Python environment. By leveraging the flexibility of its source code, developers can customize the server to handle specific connection requirements or integrate it into larger security and networking projects.

The genuine python.exe file is an essential software component developed by the Python Software Foundation that functions as the primary executable used to launch Python applications. As an adaptable, high-level programming language, Python accommodates multiple coding paradigms, including object-oriented, imperative, functional, and procedural programming styles.

PyXie is a versatile Remote Access Trojan (RAT) created using the Python programming language and packaged as a single executable file for easy distribution. Once it infects a computer, it grants an attacker extensive capabilities for surveillance and control. The malware is designed to steal sensitive information through functions like keylogging, credential harvesting, and cookie theft. It can also actively monitor its environment by recording audio and scanning the network for other devices. To maintain control and further compromise the system, PyXie can inject malicious code into web pages, run arbitrary commands from the attacker, and cover its tracks by clearing logs.

RansomEXX is a ransomware family that targeted multiple large companies starting in 2020. A little after the first wave of infections, a Linux variant of the ransomware started spreading as well. The actors behind RansomEXX seem to be after big corporations to extort as much money as possible. 

RansomEXX bears resemblances with the Defray777 ransomware. The Linux version is a simple piece of malware. It does not contain any code to terminate processes like security software, does not wipe free space like the Windows version does, and does not communicate with a command and control server. 

Infections usually occur by the actors gaining a foothold within a target infrastructure and compromising as many systems as possible before manually installing the ransomware. 

If the victim pays the ransom, they will receive both a Linux and Windows decryptor with the corresponding RSA-4096 private key and encrypted file extension embedded in the executable. The Linux decryptor is named 'decryptor64' and is a command-line driven decryptor.

Redline Stealer, obtainable as both a standalone application and through a subscription model on underground forums, functions as an information-stealing malware. It extracts and exfiltrates a wide array of data, encompassing system information, credentials, autocomplete data, and credit card information from browsers, FTP and IM clients. Additionally, the malware pilfers cryptocurrency and possesses the capability to download supplementary files onto the compromised device.

REPTILE is a backdoor utility that listens for a specialized packet for activation.

Source: Mandiant

Reptile is an open-source rootkit that uses a kernel module to hide files, directories, processes, and network connections.

Source: Trend Micro

RIFLESPINE is a cross-platform backdoor that leverages Google Drive to transfer files and execute commands. It adopts the CryptoPP library to implement the AES algorithm to encrypt and decrypt the data transmitted between an affected machine and the threat actor.

Source: Google

RootRot is a web shell written in Perl embedded into a legitimate Connect Secure .ttc file located at /data/runtime/tmp/tt/setcookie.thtml.ttc by exploiting CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887.

Source: Mandiant

Loads and runs 32-bit dynamic-link libraries (DLLs). There are no configurable settings for Rundll32. Help information is provided for a specific DLL you run with the rundll32 command.

You must run the rundll32 command from an elevated command prompt. To open an elevated command prompt, click Start, right-click Command Prompt, and then click Run as administrator. Source: Microsoft

The command-line tool Schtasks.exe allows administrators to manage scheduled tasks on both local and remote Windows systems, providing the ability to create, delete, query, modify, execute, and terminate them. It is primarily used to automate the running of programs or scripts at designated dates and times. Additionally, executing the command without any specific arguments or parameters will simply output the current status and the next scheduled execution time for all registered tasks on the machine.
SEAELF is the installer component for the MEDUSA open-source rootkit.

The sed command in UNIX stands for stream editor and it can perform lots of functions on file like searching, find and replace, insertion or deletion.

Source: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sed-command-in-linux-unix-with-examples/

This fast, highly configurable IPv4/IPv6 scanner can streamline many of your network support procedures. Its well-designed interface, light weight and portability coupled with an extensive range of options and advanced features make SoftPerfect Network Scanner an invaluable tool, whether you are a professional system administrator, someone providing occasional network maintenance, or a general user interested in computer security.

SoftPerfect Network Scanner can ping computers, scan ports, discover shared folders and retrieve practically any information about network devices via WMI, SNMP, HTTP, SSH and PowerShell. It also scans for remote services, registry, files and performance counters; offers flexible filtering and display options and exports NetScan results to a variety of formats from XML to JSON.

(source: [SoftPerfect](https://www.softperfect.com/products/networkscanner/))

SparkGateway is a legitimate component of the Ivanti Connect Secure appliance that enables remote access protocols over a browser, such as RDP or SSH. The functionality of SparkGateway can be extended through plugins.

Source: Mandiant

The SRWare Iron browser is based on the Chromium-source and offers the same features as Chrome - but without the critical points that the privacy concern.

Source: https://www.srware.net/iron/

The ssh command establishes a secure, encrypted connection between two computers across an insecure network. This connection can be used for terminal access, transferring files, and creating secure tunnels for other applications.

SystemBC is a malware as a service (MaaS) remote access trojan that was identified in early 2019. Its presence has been identified in large scale compromises such as the attack that affected the Colonial Pipline. SystemBC utilizes the TOR network to anonymize communication with C2 servers where it gathers further instruction as well as additional malware payloads. SystemBC has dropped other malwares such as ConalStrike, Mimikatz, Ryuk and Egregor and in recent attacks involving SystemBC it has been used as a secondary persistence backdoor.

mitre-attack: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder - T1547.001
Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification - T1222.001

TABLEFLIP is a passive utility to setup network traffic redirection from a specific IP address destined to the FortiManager on TCP port 541 to another specified port.

Source: Mandiant

The tar command is one of the essential commands as far as file management is concerned. It’s short for Tape Archive, and it’s used for creating & extracting archive files.  An archive file is a compressed file containing one or multiple files bundled together for more accessible storage and portability.

Source: https://linuxhint.com/linux-tar-command/

Telegram is a global instant messaging service that is utilized by threat actors and other users for various malicious and benign purposes. Among the many features telegram provides to its no malicious clients, the API and BOT functionalities can and is abused by threat actors as means to deploy malware and/or exfiltrate data. Due to the service's high usage it is often unblocked and not monitored, providing to an attacker an easy way to bypass network restrictions.

THINCRUST is a backdoor enabling the threat actor to execute commands, write files to disk, and read files from disk depending on the cookies provided in the POST request.

Source: Mandiant

ThinSpool is a dropper written in shell script that writes the web shell LightWire to a legitimate CS file. ThinSpool will re-add the malicious web shell code to legitimate files after an update.

Source: Mandiant

TINYSHELL is a lightweight client/server clone of the standard remote shell tools (rlogin, telnet, ssh, etc.), which can act as a backdoor and provide remote shell execution as well as file transfers.

Source: Mandiant

Tor is a software suite and network that provides increased anonymity on the Internet. It creates a multi-hop proxy network and utilizes multilayer encryption to protect both the message and routing information. Tor utilizes "Onion Routing," in which messages are encrypted with multiple layers of encryption; at each step in the proxy network, the topmost layer is decrypted and the contents forwarded on to the next node until it reaches its destination.

Source: MITRE

In computing, touch is a command used to update the access date and/or modification date of a computer file or directory.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_(command)

Tox is a open-source global instant messaging service that is being utilized by threat actors and other users for both malicious and benign purposes. It has various functionalities such as screen sharing, file sharing, Instant messaging, peer-to-peer network, end-to-end network, voice and video calling. This tool can be misused by threat actors for achieving their objectives.

Source: Tox

TrickBot is an advanced Trojan that emerged in 2016 as a banking Trojan before expanding into a versatile spyware tool and becoming one of the most widespread forms of malware by 2020. Because of its highly customizable design, individual infections can vary significantly, performing malicious functions ranging from credential harvesting and keylogging to data exfiltration and network reconnaissance. The malware spreads primarily through targeted spear phishing emails containing malicious links or attachments, and it is privately distributed among high-level criminal networks rather than sold openly online.

TrueSightKiller is a CPP AV/EDR Killer. This driver can be used in Windows 23H2 with HVCI enabled, loldrivers blocklist, or WDAC enabled. HVCI is designed to ensure the integrity of code executed in the kernel, but it cannot protect against all possible vulnerabilities or actions that can be performed through drivers or system interfaces.

Source: https://github.com/MaorSabag/TrueSightKiller

uname is used to print system information.

Source: https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/51680/

Vatet is a specialized malware loader designed to run malicious shellcode on a compromised system. To evade detection by security software, the shellcode it uses is first concealed using a simple XOR encoding scheme. Vatet can then retrieve this encoded payload from a file located either on the infected machine's local disk or from a shared folder on the network, after which it decodes and executes the shellcode in memory.

Veeam Credential Recovery are scripts for recovering passwords from the Veeam Backup and Replication credential manager.

Source: https://github.com/sadshade/veeam-creds

VIRTUALGATE (Windows) is a utility program written in C that is comprised of two (2) parts, a dropper, and the payload. The memory only dropper deobfuscates a second stage DLL payload that uses VMware's virtual machine communication interface (VMCI) sockets to run commands on a guest virtual machine from a hypervisor host, or between guest virtual machines on the same host.

Source: Mandiant

VIRTUALPEER is a utility used by the suspected China-nexus cyber espionage actor UNC3886.

Source: Google

VIRTUALPIE (VMware ESXi) is a lightweight backdoor written in Python that spawns a daemonized IPv6 listener on a hardcoded port on a VMware ESXi server. It supports arbitrary command line execution, file transfer capabilities, and reverse shell capabilities. Communications use a custom protocol and are encrypted using RC4.

Source: Mandiant

VIRTUALPITA (LINUX) is a backdoor which listens on TCP port 7475 and is persistent as an init.d startup service on Linux vCenter systems.  The malware is capable of arbitrary command execution, file transfer capabilities and the ability to start/stop vmsyslogd.

Source: Mandiant

VIRTUALPITA (VMware ESXi) is a 64-bit passive backdoor that establishes a listener on a fixed port of a VMware ESXi server. To avoid detection, it often imitates legitimate VMware services by using similar service names and port numbers. This backdoor allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands, upload and download files, and manage the vmsyslogd service. When executing commands, it sets the HISTFILE environmental variable to 0, preventing its actions from being recorded in the command history. Certain versions of this malware have been found to listen on a Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) and log their activity to a file named sysclog.

VIRTUALSHINE is a simple VMware VMCI sockets-based backdoor that provides access to a bash shell. VIRTUALSHINE connects to a specified target, which streams the bash pty.

Source: Google

VIRTUALSPHERE is the controller part of a simple VMCI-based backdoor. The malware transmits the second command-line argument over the VMCI socket to the server running inside the target VM.

Source: Google

VMware PowerCLI is a command-line and scripting tool built on Windows PowerShell, and provides more than 800 cmdlets for managing and automating VMware vSphere, VMware Cloud Director, vRealize Operations Manager, vSAN, VMware NSX-T Data Center, VMware Cloud Services, VMware Cloud on AWS, VMware HCX, VMware Site Recovery Manager, and VMware Horizon environments.
Source: VMware

VMware Tools provides a collection of specialized utilities and drivers that enhance the overall performance and administration of virtual machines. By installing these components within a guest operating system, users gain access to improved graphical responsiveness and more efficient resource handling between the host and the virtual environment. This integration facilitates smoother mouse movements and better clock synchronization while allowing the virtualization platform to communicate more effectively with the underlying software for streamlined maintenance and operation.

VMware vCenter is advanced server management software that provides a centralized platform for controlling your VMware vSphere environments, allowing you to automate and deliver a virtual infrastructure across the hybrid cloud with confidence.

Source: VMware

The Volatility Framework is a completely open collection of tools, implemented in Python under the GNU General Public License, for the extraction of digital artifacts from volatile memory (RAM) samples. The extraction techniques are performed completely independent of the system being investigated but offer visibilty into the runtime state of the system. The framework is intended to introduce people to the techniques and complexities associated with extracting digital artifacts from volatile memory samples and provide a platform for further work into this exciting area of research.

Source: https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility

VPN Unlimited is a service that provides a secure and private internet connection. It encrypts user data, hides their real IP address, and allows them to bypass local restrictions. The service has a strict no-logs policy, meaning it does not store information about users' online activities. VPN Unlimited offers a variety of features, including a kill switch, DNS leak protection, and a wide range of server locations. It is available on all major platforms, including Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android.

WarpWire is a credential harvester written in Javascript that is embedded into a legitimate Connect Secure file. The malware targets plaintext passwords and usernames which are submitted via a HTTP GET request to a command and control (C2) server.

Source: Mandiant

WatchDog is a simple utility that uses the `watchdog` library to monitor file system changes. When executed, it takes directory paths as command-line arguments and observes them for any activity. If an event, such as the creation, deletion, or modification of a file, occurs within the specified directories, the program logs the details of that change.

wbadmin enables users to back up and restore the operating system, volumes, files, folders, and applications from a command prompt.
Source: Microsoft

wevtutil enables users to retrieve information about event logs and publishers. You can also use this command to install and uninstall event manifests, to run queries, and to export, archive, and clear logs.

Source: Microsoft

whoami displays user, group and privileges information for the user who is currently logged on to the local system. If used without parameters, whoami displays the current domain and user name.
Source: Microsoft

WireFire is a web shell written in Python that exists as trojanized logic to a component of the Connect Secure appliance. The malware supports downloading files to the compromised device and executing arbitrary commands.

Source: Mandiant

WMIC is a legitimate windows command-line utility (Wmic.exe) to access the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). Previously, an end user would generally write a script to gather information by means of WMI. Wmic.exe can only be used by the local system administrators regardless of WMI namespace permissions on the local machine

Reference: Microsoft
wzshiming sshd is an open-source SSH server.

xdotool lets you simulate keyboard input and mouse activity, move and resize windows, etc. It does this using X11’s XTEST extension and other Xlib functions.

Source: https://www.semicomplete.com/projects/xdotool/

The yum-versionlock plugin provides a mechanism for restricting specified packages to defined versions by excluding all alternative iterations from the update process. By maintaining this fixed state, the tool ensures that critical software remains at a verified version even when newer updates become available through the repository, thereby preventing unintended configuration changes or compatibility issues during routine system maintenance.

ZipLine is a passive backdoor designed to hijack the exported accept function within the libsecure.so library. Upon invocation, the malware resolves the legitimate version of the function from libc to intercept network traffic while maintaining standard system operations. When an incoming connection is registered, ZipLine verifies that the process name is web and then inspects up to 21 bytes of data from the connected host to identify a specific trigger string. If this buffer matches the predefined sequence, the malware activates its malicious core and proceeds to receive an encrypted header containing instructions for command execution.
